key_insight: Wind and solar modelling choices barely change drought frequency or stress timing, but can shift the capacity needed to withstand those droughts by up to 480 GW.
engineering_relevance: Resilient net-zero European power system planning requires testing weather-to-power assumptions, not just selecting representative weather years.
method: Compare bias correction, wind speed extrapolation, capacity layouts, turbine and photovoltaic configurations, and wake losses.
Trace their effects on renewable energy droughts and net-zero European power system design.
Evaluate low-generation periods alongside average output.
evidence_signal: Using 85 years of reanalysis data, the study finds modelling-driven capacity shifts comparable to the spread across the most critical weather years.
watch_item: Weather-to-power inputs need regional validation; matching mean generation alone may not capture performance during droughts.
paper_title: Which wind and solar modelling choices matter? Effects on capacity factors, energy droughts and European power system configuration
